overall_reason: A studio's article page on its own Webflow system, carried by real brand work (NimbleFest mood board, lanyards, badges, speaker portraits, the live site with its Ghent date) and a named author; the design reads chosen. What reads default is the prose cadence inside the article and the sales chrome around it (gradient promo bar, 'unlock' CTA band).

findings.evidence: Failed T-OVER-CORRECTION: the prose leans on model cadence: 'The question isn't whether this is a trend. It obviously is. The question is why...', 'Let me be direct about something...', 'this isn't a nostalgia movement. This isn't Gen Z wanting... This is something stranger and more deliberate.', 'This isn't random aesthetic preference. It's a coordinated signal about five things:', 'The implication is clear.', 'Not making machines feel warm. Making the organizations...', fragment runs 'Heritage typography. Craft traditions. The texture of film photography. Hand-drawn marks.'
findings.before: "This isn't random aesthetic preference. It's a coordinated signal about five things:"
findings.after: State the claim directly with the author's own evidence: 'In our NimbleFest brief to Ruben, five signals came up:'
findings.why: An article arguing against artificial sameness undercuts itself when its sentences use the most recognisable generated rhythms.

findings.evidence: Full-width cyan-to-blue-to-violet gradient strip reading 'Discovery our cutting-edge AI offering →' (typo 'Discovery' for 'Discover'), directly above an article about rejecting the polished AI look.
findings.before: "Discovery our cutting-edge AI offering →" on a #2fdbfb→#2442bb→#726fb0 gradient
findings.after: 'Discover our AI offering →' in the site's black/white button style, or drop the bar on editorial pages.
findings.why: The one stock AI-gradient element on the page is also its first pixel row, and carries slop diction ('cutting-edge').

findings.where: CTA band after the byline, 1440 tile 10
findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER: 'Agentic organizations don't wait, they build.' / 'Start your GenAI Discovery Track and unlock easier, smarter experiences.' fits any AI consultancy; it does not follow from the article's argument.
findings.after: Tie the band to the piece: 'Want the NimbleFest brief? Talk to Stef.' with the Discover GenAI Track button.
findings.why: Stock CTA copy after a long first-person essay reads as a pasted template block.

findings.evidence: T-THREE-LINE: figures such as 'Meltwater shows 54% negative response', 'The Human Flourishing Lab found that 77% of Americans...', 'Allianz's brand value grew 20% to $28.2 billion' are attributed to sources but not linked; a reader cannot check them.
findings.before: "Consumer sentiment research from Meltwater shows 54% negative response..."
findings.after: Link each statistic to its source report.
findings.why: Unlinked round statistics in an essay about trust read as filler proof.

strengths: The NimbleFest mood-board bento is real, specific brand work: 'Bar Bricolage' stickers, a lanyard, a badge for 'Romy Goossenaerts', 'Averia Serif Libre' specimen, a Ghent warehouse photo, polaroids.
First-person, named, and situated: 'The brief we gave our designer, Ruben...', 'I'm a psychologist by training', clients named (Helan, Attentia, Energie.be).
The article honestly flags its own risk ('When Humanity Becomes Another Template') and shows the AI image tool used to make the speaker portraits rather than hiding it.
not_investigated: Sweep look_family 'violet-gradient' rests on the promo bar gradient and scattered radii; the article body itself does not show that family.
Whether the speaker portraits are generated (the article shows an AI workflow canvas of portrait variations); not judged as fake people because the article discloses the process.
